2 جشّمهُ الأَمْرَ (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. تَجْشِيمٌ; (S;) and ↓ اجشمهُ ; (S, Msb, K;) He imposed upon him, or made him to undertake, the affair, as a task, or in spite of difficulty or trouble or inconvenience; or he ordered, required, or constrained, him to do the thing, it being difficult or troublesome or inconvenient. (S, Msb, K.) Hence, (S, TA,) in a trad. of Zeyd Ibn-'Amr Ibn-Nufeyl, (TA,) “↓ مَهْمَا تُجَشِّمْنِى فَإِنِّى جَاشِمُ
” [Whatever thou impose upon me, in spite of difficulty &c., I undertake it, in spite of difficulty &c.]. (S, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
